assertion_independence: No assertion compares a value against the variable the test handed in: the byte allowance is built from fixture constants, whether a record was actually parsed is asserted separately, and both summary comparisons use observe_stream over lines the test read from the file (line 190) or a fresh whole read of the kept records (line 265). The one durability gap is not a self-comparison but a missing guard: nothing asserts that a whole request over a held whole entry parses only the appended bytes, so the regression at reckon/_backends.py:3776 cannot redden any test.

assertion_reviews.failure_condition: A fixture smaller than the 32 MB byte bound makes the case vacuous, and shrinking STREAM_COUNT or STREAM_BYTES reddens it.
Any second pass that re-parses a stream from its first byte reddens it; negative-control-base.log shows 125,562,900 B against the 36,000 B allowance with EXIT=1.
A cache that answers the second pass from held records without parsing anything would satisfy the byte allowance while proving nothing; this counter-assertion reddens on it.
A resumed summary that forgets the records read before its cursor, or folds the append twice, disagrees with observe_stream over the test's own read of the file.

assertion_reviews.assertion: assert [event['message']['id'] for event in whole] == [f'msg_{index:06d}' for index in range(43)]
assertion_reviews.failure_condition: A whole request answered from the three-record tail reddens it; negative-control-repairs.log records exactly that tail for a stream of 43 records.
A resume that seeks past the end of a truncated stream and returns the carried state unchanged reddens it; negative-control-resume-bound.log records that failure.

assertion_reviews.assertion: assert (events, malformed) == (whole, whole_malformed) or any((events, malformed) == (gained[start:], 0) for start in range(len(gained)))
assertion_reviews.failure_condition: An answer carrying a stale record, repeating one it did not append, or dropping one it did reddens it (negative-control-dropped-record.log shows the empty answer); a suffix starting later than the read's true boundary passes.

findings.text: blocking: cursor = None if whole else _STREAM_CURSORS.get(key) drops the join for every whole request, so a whole entry the cache holds is discarded on any growth and the stream is re-read from byte 0; at b3a277e1 the same entry was joined from the appended bytes, so reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1197 and reckon/crew/recovery_stream.py:837 now parse whole logs on every growth, and the same whole=True is passed by reckon/_backends.py:4042, :4123 and :4157.

non-blocking: cache_present = key in _STREAM_CURSORS or key in _PARSED_STREAMS suppresses the caller-carried resume for any stream this process holds a cursor for, so a carried resume falls through to the whole read at :4633 instead of resuming from the offset the callers at reckon/crew/recovery_stream.py:604 and reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:3647 carry.

non-blocking: _STREAM_CURSORS is a second count-bounded per-path resume store beside _STREAM_SUMMARIES at :3876, and _STREAM_WATCH_LIMIT at :3738 copies the 2048 literal of _STREAM_SUMMARY_LIMIT at :3877; the plan review's duplicate_owner-1 named _STREAM_SUMMARIES as the owner to extend.

non-blocking: the node edited this assertion to accept any suffix of the records the test appended, and no arm at head names this file - baseline_suite and after_suite both omit it and the only log that runs it, negative-control-dropped-record.log, is a mutation failure - so the loosened assertion has no recorded green run.
